author: Grace Chen
title: Aspirus Breaks Ground on Chippewa Falls Hospital to Fill Critical Care Gaps
text:
Aspirus Health facility in chippewa Falls CHIPPEWA FALLS, Wis. – Aspirus Health broke ground on a new 35,000-square-foot hospital and clinic in Chippewa Falls on Aug. 14. The facility, slated to open in September 2026, is a direct response to the healthcare void created by the closure of two regional hospitals in 2024. The project is located on a 22-acre site along Chippewa Crossing Boulevard.
Did you know? – Chippewa Falls and surrounding communities experienced a significant loss of local healthcare access when two hospitals closed in 2024, forcing residents to travel longer distances for care. The new hospital aims to expand local healthcare access and address a critical shortage of medical services. Aspirus Health, having recently expanded services in Stanley and Medford, views this Chippewa Falls facility as a long-term solution for both current and future healthcare demands. Matt Heywood, President and CEO of Aspirus Health, emphasized the organization’s commitment to the community. “We listened to the community, and this project directly answers what you’ve told us: you want more local health care options, and you deserve the very best,” he said. Jason Troxell, Aspirus Wisconsin Northwest Region President, added that the expansion will also boost the local economy.
Pro tip: – Modular construction, where parts of the building are prefabricated off-site, can substantially speed up project timelines and reduce disruptions to the surrounding community. The first phase of construction will include an emergency department with 10 treatment rooms, 10 inpatient beds, a 12-treatment-room clinic, imaging services (X-ray and CT scans), laboratory services, a pharmacy, and a helipad for emergency transport. Aspirus partnered with Boldt as the general contractor, HGA for architectural and engineering, and REI for civil engineering. Bildt, a Boldt subsidiary, will prefabricate approximately 30% of the facility, potentially accelerating the opening by three months. Sid Sczygelski, Senior vice President of Special Projects for Aspirus Health, stated the project aligns with the organization’s overall strategy.
Reader question: – What specific types of specialized care do you anticipate offering at the new hospital in the future,beyond the initial phase? Why: Aspirus Health is building the new hospital to address a critical shortage of healthcare services in Chippewa Falls and the surrounding area,which was exacerbated by the closure of two hospitals in 2024.
Who: Aspirus Health is the organization leading the project, with key partners including Boldt (general contractor), HGA (architectural and engineering), and REI (civil engineering). The project is intended to serve the residents of Chippewa Falls and the surrounding communities.
What: A new 35,000-square-foot hospital and clinic is being constructed, featuring an emergency department, inpatient beds, a clinic, imaging services, a laboratory, a pharmacy, and a helipad.
How: The project began with a groundbreaking ceremony on Aug. 14, 2024, and is utilizing a modular construction approach to accelerate the timeline.The hospital is expected to open in September 2026.
How did it end?: The project is currently underway, with the first phase of construction in progress. The hospital is scheduled to open in september 2026, providing much-needed healthcare services to the community.
